Hi Jared / Priyanka —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for inference. Attaching a short onboarding checklist and our runbook template to kick off the observability and ops scope for your integration. For the kickoff call I propose we cover: dashboards (SLO-focused), tracing hooks for end-to-end request flow, error taxonomy mapping, alert routing & escalation playbook, and a handoff of the runbook to your on-call team.

Quick proposed agenda (30–45m):
- Introductions & scope (5m)
- Current telemetry + data sources you have (5m)
- Dashboards & SLO targets (10m)
- Tracing hooks / instrumentation checklist (10m)
- Alert routing & initial runbook ownership (5m)

Please confirm availability for a kickoff Tuesday 9/16 10:00–10:45 PT or Wednesday 9/17 11:00–11:45 PT. I attached: obs_onboarding_checklist.pdf and runbook-template.md.

Next steps after kickoff: Redwood will stage a dashboards draft, provide tracing snippet examples, and populate the runbook with initial on-call play actions and escalation contacts.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan

Tessa —

Thanks, this looks great. Tuesday 9/16 10:00 PT works for us. A couple items to call out before the call so we can be prepared:

1) Dashboards: Our infra team uses Datadog and Splunk; we can forward current dashboards but we want Redwood widgets that map to request latency (p50/p95), inference errors by type, token-cost per request, and model-fallback rates.

2) Tracing: we use OpenTelemetry (OTel) collector v0.70. We need a small snippet we can drop into our request path to capture trace ids and span attributes for model selection and cache hits.

3) Alerts / Escalation: We’d like a first-pass suggestion for alert severities and routing (pager vs slack) for the following: sustained p95>500ms for 5min, error-rate >2% for 10min, and model-fallback rate >1% for 5min. Also please include who at Acme should be listed as primary and secondary on the runbook (we’ll confirm names).

We’ll invite our infra lead and on-call for the kickoff.

—Jared
Senior Platform Engineer
Acme Analytics
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Lopez <jared.lopez@acme-analytics.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability & Ops: Kickoff and runbook / dashboard roadmap

Jared —

Thanks for the details. Attaching a quick tracing snippet and a mapping for the dashboard widgets below. I’ll paste the lightweight OTel snippet you can run in your request middleware; it emits trace.id and the following attributes: redwood.model, redwood.model_variant, redwood.kv_cache_hit (bool), redwood.batch_size.

--- tracing middleware (pseudo):
function injectRedwoodTrace(ctx, req) {
  const span = tracer.startSpan('redwood.request', { kind: 'client' });
  span.setAttribute('redwood.model', req.modelName);
  span.setAttribute('redwood.model_variant', req.variant || 'default');
  span.setAttribute('redwood.kv_cache_hit', req.kvCacheHit ? true : false);
  span.setAttribute('redwood.batch_size', req.batchSize || 1);
  // ensure trace id is returned in response header X-Trace-Id
  ctx.setResponseHeader('X-Trace-Id', span.context().traceId);
  return next();
}

--- Dashboard widget mapping (first-pass):
- Latency: p50, p95 time-series (per-model filter)
- Error breakdown: 5xx vs client errors vs model-fallbacks (stacked)
- Cost: tokens per request, avg tokens per model
- Cache hit ratio: kv_cache_hit% and impact on latency
- Model variant routing: percentage of requests per variant

Alert routing suggestion (first-pass):
- Sev 1 (Pager): sustained p95 > 750ms for 10m OR error-rate > 5% for 5m
- Sev 2 (Slack + Email): p95 > 500ms for 5m OR error-rate > 2% for 10m
- Sev 3 (Slack digest): model-fallback rate > 1% for 5m or cache hit ratio drop > 15%

I’ll turn these into concrete Datadog query templates before the kickoff. Also, we recommend adding enrichment to alerts with the last X trace ids and a link to the request payload (if allowed by your data policy).

—Marcus
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
